name: Adam Zhang

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What does a normal day look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and came into this junior accounting job with a bachelor’s degree in accounting. I enter invoices, prepare simple tax returns and use a paper tick list because I still mix up some codes. Mira, my supervisor, checks my files; I have never used an AI tool and would rather master the process I can explain. I like making a client’s figures balance, but repeating the same tax-code mistake is frustrating.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is your day like after you leave the office?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I collect our two children from school, then Lin, my partner, comes home from the clinic reception desk. We have a mortgage, about three months of expenses saved, and my pay is typical for this junior role. There are some similar jobs nearby, though changing jobs with a family is not a small choice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a little automation will not change who checks a tax return. I want our names on the file so a client knows who to ask when a figure is wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We have about three months of expenses saved and my pay is ordinary for a junior accountant, so the mortgage feels manageable if shifts stay steady. I still wonder whether the easiest invoice entries will quietly leave my desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep entering the invoices and checking each return against my paper tick list. In the first year I would ask my supervisor Mira for a paid walk-through if a new check becomes required in writing, but I would keep using the current approved process until then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about a small change touching the part of the job I am still learning. Our bills are covered, so I am not lying awake over it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is on that tick list?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It has the missing-receipt questions and the tax codes I tend to mix up. Mira, my supervisor, signs off my work and adds a note when I need to redo something.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you try an AI tool on your own?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used an AI tool and would not put a client file into a new tool myself. If the firm requires one, I need a paid demonstration on an old file and written instructions.

say: I would keep **named sign-off** on tax returns even if routine entry speeds up.
I would tell clients a **person** still answers for wrong figures.
think: Our **three-month cushion** makes the mortgage manageable while shifts hold.
I wonder whether easy **invoice entries** will leave my junior desk.
do: Keep entering **client invoices** and checking returns with my paper tick list.
Take a **paid tool walk-through** only after a written job requirement.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about routine tasks moving while our bills remain covered.
S0.quote: I have never used an AI tool and would not put a client file into a new tool myself.
fieldNote: His **paper list** tracks the codes and missing receipts he personally gets wrong; it supports careful junior learning.
He has **three months saved** and steady pay; a new tool needs a written job rule and paid demonstration.

steps.text: Keep entering client invoices and checking returns with paper tick list
Take paid tool walkthrough only after written job requirement

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to name the reviewer who checks each automated draft. I would also ask what junior accountants are meant to learn if software does the first pass.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing tax notes and checking simple accounts are much of my day, so my hours could shrink as those tasks move. We can cover the mortgage for about three months, and some local firms hire accountants, but I do not know whether they need another junior.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask Mira for the roster forecast and keep doing the current review work. If the firm makes its approved checker part of my written job and pays for a demonstration, I would learn it on old returns; in the first year, if my hours are actually cut, I would apply for advertised local junior accounting posts while keeping the paid shifts I have.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a possible cut, but I can still make choices if it comes. I do not expect to lose the whole wage tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask Mira to show you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask her to show which error the checker catches and what it misses on an old client return. Then I could add the new check to my paper list instead of guessing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you apply before hours are cut?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would look at postings, but I would not tell another firm I could start before I have an offer and a start date. Our mortgage needs the current wage until a replacement is real.

say: I would demand a **named reviewer** on every automated draft.
I would ask how **junior accountants** learn when first-pass work moves.
think: My **simple account checks** could mean fewer hours under steady disruption.
Three months saved and **some local firms** give us limited room to respond.
do: Request a **roster forecast** and keep paid reviews while hours hold.
Learn the **approved checker** on old returns only with written job rule and paid demonstration.
After an actual cut, apply to **advertised local junior posts** without leaving current shifts first.
feel: I feel **anxious** about possible lost hours, with some time to respond.
S1.quote: Our mortgage needs the current wage until a replacement is real.
fieldNote: He distinguishes **possible lost hours** from an immediate dismissal and does not claim catastrophe in the milder scenario.
His **job search** starts after a cut, and he protects current pay until an offer and start date are real.

steps.text: Keep paid account reviews while asking supervisor for roster forecast
Learn approved checker on old returns only with written rule and paid demonstration
Apply to advertised local junior posts after cut while retaining shifts until offer and start date

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2028 reaches tax and account screens in 2028; the capable robots around 2031 come too late to protect office jobs. The firm should tell junior staff what hours it expects to keep.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect most of my junior review shifts to go when cheaper AGI can do the thinking work. Our three-month cushion would run down quickly against the mortgage. Nearby firms may have fewer openings at the same time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask for written notice of any shift cut and stop the paid children’s activity club at the next renewal to hold the fee in our account. If my shifts fall in the first year after 2028, I would apply to advertised local accounting posts and ask my partner Lin whether confirmed extra clinic shifts could carry one mortgage payment; I would not resign until another employer gives written pay and a start date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed by likely lost shifts and the mortgage clock. I do have a list of calls, but no job offer yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Lin take extra clinic shifts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Lin is a clinic receptionist and sometimes covers leave, but those shifts depend on the rota. We would count them only when the clinic confirms the hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you tell the children about the club?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our two school-age children the club stops next term and we can use the public playground instead. I would not ask them to solve an adult bill.

say: I would say **AGI by 2028** hits tax screens before capable robots arrive.
I would ask the firm for **written shift notice**.
think: I expect most **junior review shifts** to go after 2028.
Our **three-month cushion** would shrink quickly against the mortgage.
do: Stop the **children’s paid club** at renewal and retain the fee for bills.
After lost shifts, apply to **advertised local posts** while keeping paid work until a written offer and start date.
Ask **partner Lin** about confirmed clinic shifts for one mortgage payment after cuts.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by likely lost shifts and a fixed mortgage.
S2.quote: Our three-month cushion would run down quickly against the mortgage.
fieldNote: His **first-pass desk work** is exposed in 2028, so he does not treat the three-year robot delay as a reprieve.
He counts **Lin’s clinic shifts** only when confirmed and keeps current pay until a new employer provides written terms and start date.

steps.text: Stop paid children’s club at renewal and retain fee for bills
Apply to advertised local posts after cuts; keep paid shifts until written offer and start date
Ask partner Lin about confirmed clinic shifts for one mortgage payment

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my colleagues AGI by 2031 gives us five years to ask what work the firm will still pay people to do. The robots around 2034 do not change our account-screen date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might build another few months of savings by 2031, but the junior tax checks still look exposed. I would rather train in a nearby task I have seen than pay for an unknown course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask Mira whether the firm will pay for payroll training, including study hours, and enrol only if fees and paid time are approved in writing. I would save 65 a month while both wages hold; in the first year after 2031, if my review shifts fall, I would take a vacant payroll post only with written salary and hours at least equal to now, or keep the remaining shifts while applying for advertised local jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, with a few years to make the numbers work. The payroll plan still depends on funding and a vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Mira cannot get training funded?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep reviewing accounts and ask a local firm about a posted paid payroll trainee job. I would not use our mortgage savings for tuition.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do you save 65 a month?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would stop buying coffee on school-run mornings and move the amount after payday. If Lin’s or my shifts fall, the transfer would pause.

say: I would use the **2031 runway** to ask what paid work remains.
I would remind colleagues the **2034 robot date** does not protect account screens.
think: My **junior tax checks** still look exposed in 2031.
Extra **mortgage savings** need both household wages to keep arriving every month.
do: Enrol in **payroll training** with written fees and paid hours; if refused, keep reviews and seek posted paid trainee work.
Save **65 monthly** while both household wages hold.
After lost shifts, take a **vacant payroll post** with written equal pay and hours or apply locally while keeping paid reviews.
feel: I feel **anxious** because funding and a vacancy are uncertain.
S3.quote: I would not use our mortgage savings for tuition.
fieldNote: He sets **written funding** for any payroll course and keeps existing account shifts if the firm cannot pay.
His **65 monthly transfer** pauses if either wage falls, and a future payroll move needs a real vacancy with equal written terms.

steps.text: Enrol in payroll training only with written fees and paid study hours
Save 65 monthly while both household wages hold
Seek posted paid payroll trainee work while keeping reviews if funding is denied
After cuts, take vacant payroll role with written equal pay/hours or apply locally while employed

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2036 gives our family time to pay down the mortgage and the firm time to train staff properly. The desk work still changes in 2036, before capable robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years could take us through the children’s school years with a lower loan balance. I still doubt there will be much junior return checking after 2036, but I could be doing payroll by then if I learn it carefully.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep checking tax returns and request one paid payroll shadow shift each quarter if Mira approves it. I would first build a four-month cash reserve while both wages hold, then pay 90 monthly against mortgage principal; in the first year after 2036, if tax hours fall, I would take a vacant payroll role only with written pay and hours no worse than now, or seek an advertised local post before leaving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the far end, but our next few years look workable. A decade gives me space to do one careful change at a time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep cash before paying the loan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A paid-down mortgage cannot buy food during a delayed payslip. Four months in cash would let us keep the children settled while we search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move cities for payroll?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not on a rumour. I would check local advertised jobs first because there are some, and I would need a written offer and start date before changing the children’s school.

say: I would use the **decade** to reduce mortgage debt and build careful skills.
I would note **desk work** changes before capable robots arrive.
think: A lower **mortgage balance** would give our family room to move.
do: Keep **tax reviews** and shadow payroll quarterly only with Mira’s approval and paid hours.
Build **four months cash**, then pay 90 monthly against principal while both wages hold.
After cuts, seek vacant **payroll work** with equal written terms or local posts; change schools only after written offer and start date.

S4.quote: A decade gives me space to do one careful change at a time.
fieldNote: His **long-run sequence** is cash before extra mortgage payments, reflecting practical household caution.
The **payroll shift** needs Mira’s approval and paid time; the later move needs a vacancy and written pay and hours.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I expect my junior review shifts to go before I have trained for another task. Written notice, paid payroll training and a genuine vacancy would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how a parent explains a lost shift on a school night. A mortgage letter is still on the table when the children have gone to bed.

headlineQuote: A mortgage letter is still on the table when the children have gone to bed.
portrait: At **43**, Adam is a junior accountant with a bachelor’s degree, still learning tax codes under his supervisor Mira.
He and **partner Lin** have two school-age children, a mortgage, typical pay and three months saved.
He has **never used AI** and prefers proven checks, though some similar accounting jobs are nearby.
The **2028 deadline** alarms him; longer runways allow paid payroll training, cash savings and a conditional role change.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove most junior review shifts before he can train for another paid role.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written notice**, funded payroll training and an actual vacancy with protected pay.
